key_insight: PINN-based, solver-agnostic training lets turbulence closures be learned directly from the RANS residual and then transferred across bluff-body shapes without tying them to a specific CFD discretization.
engineering_relevance: This offers a fast path to screen and deploy turbulence models for industrial wake flows, with better out-of-sample performance and practical training on a single GPU or even PIV data.
method: Train closures inside a PINN using automatic differentiation of the RANS equations.
Compare four closure forms: three Reynolds-stress models with realizability constraints and one direct Reynolds-force model.
Use input-gradient smoothing and a Lipschitz constraint to improve coupled stability before freezing the closure in a finite-element solver.
evidence_signal: The models were trained on six 2D bluff-body wakes at Re=10^4 and evaluated with strict leave-one-shape-out testing; the direct force model gave the best generalization and about 8.5% LOSO drag error.
watch_item: Although the learned closures are solver-agnostic in training, they still must remain stable when deployed in a conventional CFD solver, so stability checks are essential.
paper_title: Generalizable turbulence closures across bluff-body shapes by PINN-based solver-agnostic training
